summary: Independent review reproduced the original parser failures on the recorded base and the remaining Mistral no-space separator failure across whole, character, and every two-way split delivery. Exact candidate 648a8992ef222042ffac9cf931e929a1d3600427 passed the original eight-parser reproduction, its focused regression, the full function-call unit suite, and 13,424 independent adversarial Mistral deliveries without leaking tool JSON into normal_text.

tests.what_was_measured: On recorded base 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365, reproduced original one-shot/character-stream parity failures for GLM, GLM45, GLM47, Minimax-M2, and Step3.
On the recorded base, asserted that whole and character streaming lost calls after the first, leaked the remaining JSON, and all 122 two-way splits failed; the diagnostic assertion succeeded.
At exact candidate commit, all eight parsers matched one-shot parsing under character-at-a-time delivery.
29 tests passed with 2,077 subtests, including the candidate's JSON-separator whitespace regression.

64 whitespace-pair variants and 13,424 deliveries matched one-shot parsing with no normal_text leakage; covered whole, character, fixed-size, every two-way split, randomized three-way splits, nested JSON, and commas in strings.
Complete function-call unit suite: 551 tests passed with 2,098 subtests.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reviewed defect is deterministic Python string/JSON parser behavior; no model or GPU kernel is involved.

remaining_limitations: No model weights, tokenizer, HTTP serving process, semantic model accuracy, GPU kernel, multi-GPU, or distributed workload was exercised.
The prepared host is ROCm 7.2/gfx950 with PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 rather than the reporter's CUDA/RTX 4090 environment; no cross-architecture serving claim is made.
The candidate changes no native source, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
